title: Not Yet, Yam!
lines: Ted has a pet pig. It is Yam.
Yam is big and Yam can run.
Ted had a bag of yams.
"Yes, Yam! But not yet," said Ted.
But Yam ran at the bag and got it.
Yams pop up and hop on the rug.
Ted is not mad. He fed Yam ten yams.
Yam naps on the rug. Ted pats him.

questions.ask: What was in the bag Ted had?
questions.listenFor: Yams. Have your child find the word yams on the page and touch it - proving it beats remembering it.

questions.ask: Why did Yam run at the bag?
questions.listenFor: Yam had not been fed yet and wanted the yams. If they say "he was hungry," ask them to find the line that tells us - the word yet is the clue.

questions.ask: Do you think Yam is a good pet? Tell me why you think so.
questions.listenFor: No wrong answer. You want a reason from the story - Yam grabbed the bag, or Yam naps quietly at the end. Ted does not blame Yam; he works out that the pig was hungry. Reasons matter more than the yes or no.
